Committee: Military and Veterans Affairs
Sponsor: Standridge
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 02/23/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 292 as introduced would reduce pistol permit receipts to the several counties by undetermined amounts, dependent upon the number of pistol permits issued at no cost to certain military members and veterans as provided by this bill. Pistol permit fees vary throughout the state, depending on the county and the length of time the permit is valid.
Dickie Drake, Chair
Military and Veterans Affairs

Committee: Ways and Means Education
Sponsor: Brown (C)
Analyst: Daniel Davenport
Date: 03/01/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 190 as introduced allows the Public School and College Authority (PSCA) to use proceeds from the sale of bonds issued by the PSCA to pay for the cost of constructing, altering, improving, and equipping buildings and other facilities of the Dauphin Island Sea Lab for public educational purposes. This bill will not otherwise affect state or local funding.
Bill Poole, Chair
Ways and Means Education

Committee: Education Policy
Sponsor: Hanes
Analyst: Daniel Davenport
Date: 03/09/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 9 as introduced would reduce the obligations of Troy University and Alabama Agricultural and Mechanical (A&M) University by an undetermined amount by prohibiting the use of in-kind or matching funds to support institutes affiliated with the Chinese government operating on its campuses, as provided by this bill.
According to information provided by the university, Alabama A&M University's current contract with Confucius Institute, which expires in 2023, includes $150,000 in state matching funds.
Terri Collins, Chair
Education Policy
